html:
The Pulse dashboard is a Next.js App Router app with Tailwind CSS v4 and HeroUI v3 (@heroui/react + @heroui/styles). This module covers the scaffold, the component composition, and the two things that are easy to get wrong: the stylesheet import order and accessibility.

The full working project ships alongside this course as heroui-saas-dashboard/ (see the README of that repo for exact versions).

Scaffold

Add a typecheck script, because next build is not a typecheck you can iterate on:

Both must pass before you call the UI done. A dev server that renders is not the same thing — build catches type errors, invalid exports and server/client boundary mistakes that dev tolerates.

Tailwind v4: no config file

Tailwind v4 is CSS-first. There is no tailwind.config.js; configuration lives in the stylesheet via @theme.

The global stylesheet — order matters

Gotcha: importing @heroui/styles before tailwindcss compiles but silently loses component styles, because Tailwind's preflight resets them afterwards. The order is not cosmetic.

Styling with the library's variables, not overrides

HeroUI exposes spacing and radius as CSS custom properties. Use them instead of patching component internals:

Why this matters: overriding .card__body { padding: 12px } breaks the moment the library changes its internal class names, and it fights the design system's density scale. Consuming the variables keeps your layout consistent with the components and survives upgrades.

No provider in v3

HeroUI v3 does not need a provider wrapper. There is no <HeroUIProvider> to add to app/layout.tsx. If you copy a v2 tutorial that wraps the tree in a provider, delete it — at best it is dead code, at worst it duplicates context.

The compound component API

v3 components compose with dot notation. Card.Header and Card.Content are the ones that replace v2's monolithic props:

That pattern repeats for every KPI tile. Card.Header carries the label and trend; Card.Content carries the visual.

Layout: sticky header + responsive left nav

Two details that make this work:

  • lg: is Tailwind's min-width: 1024px. hidden lg:block on the aside plus lg:hidden on the trigger gives exactly the "collapses below 1024px" behaviour.
  • The sticky header needs a stacking context above the content (z-40) or cards scroll over it.

The dashboard page

The table, with accessible labelling

aria-label on <Table> gives the grid a name for screen readers, and isRowHeader on the first column makes each row announce "INV-2026-091, row 1" instead of just reading cell values. Without both, a screen-reader user hears an unnamed grid of numbers.

Select and ListBox

aria-label is required: a Select with only a placeholder has no accessible name, and a screen reader announces an unnamed combobox.

Modal and Drawer

Both Modal and Drawer handle focus trapping, Escape, and restoring focus to the trigger on close. That is a large accessibility win you get for free — do not reimplement it with a div.

Avatar and Badge

Search field

Accessibility checklist

  • Every Select, Table, Modal, Drawer and icon-only Button has an aria-label or an associated visible label.
  • Table has aria-label and isRowHeader on the first column.
  • Icon-only buttons say what they do (aria-label="Open navigation"), not what they look like.
  • Focus is visible: never outline-none without a focus-visible ring.
  • Colour is not the only signal — the invoice status has text, not just a green dot.
  • ProgressBar has an aria-label including the actual numbers.
  • Tab order follows visual order; the nav Drawer comes before main in the DOM.
  • Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for body text.

Verifying keyboard navigation

Do this by hand, in this order — it takes two minutes and catches almost everything:

Component Keys to test Expected
Select Tab to focus, Enter/Space to open menu opens, focus moves into it
Select ↓ ↑ highlight moves, announced by the screen reader
Select Enter selects, closes, focus returns to the trigger
Select Esc closes without changing the value
Table Tab focus enters the grid, arrow keys move between cells
Table Home / End first / last cell in the row
Modal Esc closes; focus returns to the button that opened it
Drawer Tab focus is trapped inside while open
Nav Tab from the header reaches the nav links in visual order

Screen-reader spot checks (VoiceOver Cmd+F5 on macOS, NVDA on Windows):

  1. The table announces its name and "row 1 of 12".
  2. The select announces "Filter by plan, combo box, All plans".
  3. The progress bar announces "Quota used: 412000 of 500000".

Wiring the API

Fetch on the server where possible: the token stays out of the browser bundle, and the first paint has data instead of a spinner.

Loading and error states

loading.tsx and error.tsx are App Router conventions — no library needed.

Exercises

  1. Confirm the stylesheet import order by swapping the two @import lines and observing the visual breakage.
  2. Add a fourth KPI tile using Card + Card.Header + Card.Content.
  3. Move every hard-coded padding to var(--spacing-*) and every radius to var(--radius-*).
  4. Add a Select + ListBox filter that actually filters the invoice table.
  5. Run the keyboard table above against your build and fix anything that fails.
  6. Add a Modal to create an invoice and a Drawer for invoice detail, both with correct focus behaviour.
  7. Confirm npm run typecheck and npm run build both pass with zero warnings.

Next: Deployment
